The US [Federal Reserve (Fed)](https://equalsmoney.com/financial-glossary/federal-reserve-system) announces its decisions regarding interest rates eight times a year during [Federal Open Market Committee (FOMC)](https://equalsmoney.com/financial-glossary/federal-open-market-committee) meetings., approximately every six weeks. [See the impact](https://equalsmoney.com/economic-calendar/events/fed-interest-rate-decision#impact). **The current**[**federal funds rate**](https://equalsmoney.com/financial-glossary/federal-funds-rate)**target range is 3.50% – 3.75%**. This can encourage consumer spending, business investment, and economic growth, while also weakening [USD](https://equalsmoney.com/currencies/majors/usd) and making exports more competitive. The frequency of rate changes varies based on economic data, financial stability, and the Fed’s [monetary policy](https://equalsmoney.com/financial-glossary/monetary-policy) goals. *   The [**effective federal funds rate (EFFR)**](https://equalsmoney.com/financial-glossary/effective-federal-funds-rate) (the actual overnight interest rate at which U.S. banks lend to each other) is currently around **3.64%**, based on the most [recent available data](https://ycharts.com/indicators/effective_federal_funds_rate) (March 2026). See below for [historical interest rate data](https://www.forbes.com/advisor/investing/fed-funds-rate-history/), showing how the Federal Funds Rate has changed over time.
